candidate.title: SELEX
candidate.scope: The assigned schematic depicts high-throughput systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (HT-SELEX) for transcription-factor DNA-binding specificity: a barcoded 14N double-stranded DNA ligand pool is selected on a well-immobilized fusion protein, recovered, amplified and sequenced to infer a binding motif. SELEX is the card-level umbrella. The verified collection page includes a broader SELEX or SELEX-seq heading but captions this same drawing specifically as HT-SELEX. SELEX-seq, the Nextera-adapter DUX4 adaptation, SELMAP, RNA aptamer selections and software discussed in surrounding sources are not drawn alternative workflows. The far-left transcription-factor-binding-site and Target sequence icons are explanatory context, not a depicted genomic-material extraction route. The horizontal selection path has no drawn branch or cycle-back arrow; successive rounds mentioned by the catalogue are not expanded into additional operations.

operations.label: Fusion protein immobilized in well

The vector and a surface-attached protein are different materials. Expression and immobilization are represented together at the resolution of the drawn arrow; no free-protein purification route is reconstructed. operations.information_effect: Presents a particular DNA-binding protein as the selection target while retaining it in the well.

method_scopes.rationale: All operations apply to the single depicted pD40htSELEX/14N well-selection implementation of HT-SELEX. This is an implementation within the broader SELEX family; it does not assert that every HT-SELEX protocol uses these tags, ligand length or immobilization. The collection heading is verified against its matching labels and HT-SELEX caption. SELEX-seq papers are assessed as related implementations rather than assigning their distinct preparation histories to this drawn route. The primary HT-SELEX association is Jolma et al., PMID 20378718, whose supplied evidence is abstract-only: it supports affinity-tagged proteins, barcoded selection oligonucleotides, multiplexed sequencing and motif readout. Fusion-vector and 14N details here are supported by the drawing and catalogue, not independently verified by that abstract.
